newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to improve disabled access to small planes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to improve disabled access to small planes.

text.p: Disabled airline passengers will receive the same help boarding small commuter planes they already get when flying bigger aircraft under new regulations announced by the U.S. Transportation Department on Friday.
The new rules will force commuter airlines and airports to provide equipment to help disabled travelers board smaller airplanes that, because of their compact cabins, have posed them most difficulty.
The rules, which apply to larger jets, will affect commuter planes with 19-30 seats and be phased in over two-to-four years, depending on the aircraft's size.
The agency said there were no rules on access for the disabled to planes with fewer than 19 seats.
